AAB: [6292] Weight (mass) of goods including packing but excluding the carrier's equipment.
AAC: Total weight of goods excluding packaging.
AAD: [6012] Total gross weight (mass) of all goods items referred to as one consignment including packaging but excluding any transport equipment.
AAF: [6048] Weight (mass) if goods without any packaging.
AAG: Force exerted by a thruster installed at the stern of a vessel.
AAH: Force exerted by a thruster installed at the bow of a vessel.
AAI: The hydrate content of an alcoholic product at the moment of bottling.
AAJ: The number of units contained on a pallet.
AAK: An indication of the fat content of a product.
AAM: [6300] The measure of the overall size of a ship determined in accordance with the provisions of the International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships, 1969.
AAN: [6302] The measure of the useful capacity of a ship determined in accordance with the provisions of the International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships, 1969.
AAP: Electromotive force, or difference of electronic potential between two points.
AAR: Measurement of the rate of dispersal of heat.
AAS: Measurement of the flow of air.
AAT: Measurement of the impact of a shock.
AAU: Temperature identified system or process works according to specifications.
AAV: Temperature identified system or process does not work according to specifications.
AAW: The volume unadjusted for factors such as temperature or gravity.
AAX: The volume after adjustment for factors such as temperature or gravity.
D: The agreed weight of despatched goods whose weight may change during transport.
N: The actual weight of the goods excluding packaging.
T: (6052) (6156) Weight excluding goods and loose accessories.
ABF: The width of an item when unrolled.
ABG: The length of an item when unrolled.
ABH: The area occupied by an item when unrolled.
ABI: Measure of the malt and hops content of beer, before fermentation has taken place.
ABJ: The amount of air space taken up by the entity identified in the 6311 qualifier.
ABL: Horizontal distance from the left most edge of the package to the center of the hole into which the peg is inserted.
ABM: Vertical distance from the top of the package to the top of the hole into which the peg is inserted.
ABN: The number of layers per pallet.
ABO: The amount of the single active chemical ingredient within a product.
ABP: Amount of product used as the basis for the specification of the chemical product strenght.
ABT: The maximum weight of a payload.
ABY: Registered summer dead weight total tonnage of the vessel.
ABZ: Total weight of containerized cargo on vessel.
RJ: Hardness in the Rockwell C scale.
BMY: The measurement of the platinum component.
BMZ: The measurement of the silver component.
ACA: Total weight of non-containerized cargo on vessel.
ACE: [4240] Endorsement of the true weight (mass) as ascertained or verified.
ACG: The weight on which charges are based.
ACN: Estimated weight (mass) of goods, including packing and excluding carrier's.
ACP: Estimated size or measure of anything in three dimensions.
ACS: Total overall length of the vessel.
ACV: [6046] (6042) (6044) The length in a vehicle, whereby the complete width and height over that length is needed for the goods.
ACW: Number of axles of movable equipment or means of transport on wheels.
ACX: The revenue-producing load carried by a means of transport.
BNA: The leaning or inclination of a vessel expressed in degrees port or starboard.
BNC: The volume of water present in a container that is not in suspension in the contained liquid.
BNE: The relative density of petroleum liquids as specified by a standard developed by the API.
BNF: The total volume of all petroleum liquids and sediment and water, excluding free water, at observed temperature and pressure.
BNG: The total volume of all petroleum liquids, sediment, and water excluding free water, corrected by the appropriate volume correction factor for the observed temperature and American Petroleum Institute relative density, or density to a standard temperature.
BNH: The change in the volume measurement.
BNI: The total volume of all petroleum liquids, excluding sediment and water and free water, corrected by the appropriate volume correction factor for the observed temperature and American Petroleum Institute gravity relative to density or to a standard temperature.
BNJ: The material in vessel tanks, void spaces, and pipelines after discharge.
BNK: The total volume of all petroleum liquids, sediment and water corrected by the appropriate volume correction factor for the observed temperature and American Petroleum Institute (API) gravity, relative density, or density to a standard temperature.
BNL: The total volume of all petroleum liquids, sediment and water and free water at observed temperature and pressure.
BNM: The measured distance from the surface of the liquid to a fixed datum plate or to the tank bottom.
BNN: The total weight of all petroleum liquids excluding sediments, water and free water.
BNO: The measurement of non-hydrocarbon solid material and water in suspension in petroleum liquid.
BNP: The observed distance from the tank bottom or datum plate to the established reference point.
BNQ: The measured distance from the tank bottom or datum plate to the established reference point.
BNR: The measured distance from the cargo liquid surface to the reference point.
BNS: The correction applied to the observed gauge or observed volume when a vessel is not on an even keel.
BNT: The distance between the bow and the bridge of a vessel.
BNU: Used to identify the peg hole if more than one hole is present in the product or packaging.
BNV: Indicates the number of non coded physical groupings (inner packs) of next lower level trade items within the current trade item level.
BNW: The number of next lower level trade items contained within the physical non-coded grouping (inner pack).
BNX: The number of trade items contained on a single layer of a pallet.
BNY: The height of a single layer of packed items.
BNZ: The weight measurement of the packing material used for skin tight covering (e.g. when packaging prepared meats, poultry, cheese, and other food products).
ADR: The starting position from the beginning of an item located in the length direction.
ADS: The end position from the beginning of an item located in the length direction.
ADT: The start position from the beginning of an item located in the width direction.
ADV: The start position from the beginning of an item located in the thickness direction.
ADW: The end position from the beginning of an item located in the thickness direction.
ADX: Actual filling weight of a transport container.
ADY: Maximum capacity of a transport container.
ADZ: The declared net weight of a product or products used for invoicing, customs or transport purposes.
TC: A measurement in relation to temperature.
TN: Measurement of a specific length of time.
AEA: Maximum height of products or packages loaded onto a given transportation device or equipment such as a pallet.
AEB: Maximum height up to which the same product or package may be placed one upon the other for storage purposes.
AEC: The calculated weight of the item based on the ordered dimensions.
AEE: The impurity of the product i.e. the measurement of other chemical elements not normally appearing in a product.
AEI: The weight of a product when all liquids used in the packaging of the product have been removed.
AEL: Extent or measure of a surface.
AEM: Maximum storage limit of the equipment.
AEN: The index of transport determines the maximum radiation level at a distance of 1m from the external surface.
AEP: Weight which is the outcome of the division of the total gross weight by the number of units.
AEQ: Depth of water from the surface of water to the bottom of the vessel measured at the draft mark of the bow.
AER: Depth of water from the surface of water to the bottom of the vessel measured at the draft mark of the stern.
AES: The quality, state, or degree of being acid.
AET: [6294] Weight of a transport equipment including the cargo and carrier's equipment.
AEU: Total weight of all transport equipment including the cargo and carrier's equipment.
AEW: Measurement of force required to drive a standard penetrating stamp.
AEX: Measurement of the elastic force using a standard penetrating stamp.
AEY: Measurement of weight of juice, based on 100 grams of the entire weight.
AEZ: Measurement of the colouring of the epidermis of a fruit.
BNB: The condition of a vessel with reference to its longitudinal axis.
AFA: The measurement of the fixed increment.
AFB: Measure of the elastic force of the pulp of a fruit. It is measured with a penetrating stamp with diameter 10.
AFC: Measure of the elastic force of the pulp of a fruit. It is measured with a penetrating stamp with diameter 25.
AFD: Measure of the elastic force of the pulp of a fruit. It is measured with a penetrating stamp with diameter 50.
AFE: The maximum weight which may be stacked upon a product or package without the product or packaging being crushed.
AFF: The total cubic space occupied by an item, taking into account any protruding components, arrived at by multiplying the maximum length, width and height.
AFG: The percentage of fat content in dry matter.
AFH: Measurement of the sugar content of a solution.
AFI: The hydrate content which occurs in an alcoholic product after bottling.
AFL: The vertical distance between the waterline and the upper edge of the deck line.
AFM: The depth of water needed to float the ship (Maximum vessel draught according to Load Line Certificate IMO, MSC/Circ. 920 15 June 1999).
AFN: Mass of the explosive part or substance of goods without any packing.
AFO: A number, assigned to fissile material i.e. material capable of sustaining a nuclear chain reaction, which is used to provide control over the accumulation of packages containing such material.
AFP: Amount of waste on board at the moment of the notification.
AFQ: Amount of waste to be delivered to a waste reception facility, e.g. in the port of call.
AFR: Estimated amount of waste to be generated between creation of the current notification and arrival in the next port of call, irrespective of use of incinerator or compactor or disposal at sea.
AFS: Amount of waste remaining on board when leaving the port of call.
AFT: The number of distinct colours represented, e.g. in an image or in a display.
AFU: The maximum number of distinct colours that can be represented, e.g. in an image or in a display.
AFV: The level of detail of an image.
AFW: The maximum level of detail produced by a device.
AFX: The portion of sound energy a surface absorbs, measured at different frequencies.
ZZZ: A code assigned within a code list to be used on an interim basis and as defined among trading partners until a precise code can be assigned to the code list.
VH: The height of the door of a van or container.
BSX: An indication of measurements in which options contained within a Customer Specific Article are available, e.g. 10 metre planks of wood may be sold in step sizes of 2 metres.
ZFS: The measured substance iron plus silicon.
VW: The width of the door of a van or container.
LN: [6168] To specify the value of a length dimension.
CHO: The temperature at which emergency response is required for self-reactive substances and organic peroxides.
BRB: Percentage of trade item components that clearly label how to facilitate product disassembly and recycling.
BRC: The percentage of the plastic components only made from rapidly renewable plant-based material by net weight of product.
BRD: The pressure that should be applied by a clamp.
BRF: Endorsement of the true volume as ascertained or verified.
BRH: Total volume of goods and/or parcels.
BRJ: Distance of vertical center of gravity relative to item's base.
BRL: Measurement of the carbon dioxide (C02) component.
BRM: The number of base units contained on a pallet.
BRN: Micro-organism colonies that are to be counted under determined conditions.
BRO: The volume of liquid which results after a dilution agent has been added, e.g. undiluted orange juice of 200ml, after dilution with water the volume of diluted liquid equals 1 litre.
BRP: A measurement of the energy efficiency of an article.
BRQ: Number of layers of a product or products within a package, container, etc.
BRR: The highest demand recorded during the period of recording of usage of the supply.
BRS: The number of pallet places needed to store or to transport pallets (can be stacked).
BRT: An indication of the net cubed measurement of a package.
BRU: The ratio of the power dissipated (active power in kW) to the total power (which is the product of the input volts times amps given in kVa). When equipment which uses reactive power is being operated the power factor will be less than one.
BRV: Maximum number of identical items stackable on top of item.
WU: The weight per unit of length.
MO: Measurement application is the moisture content of the item.
CT: In combination with the other data elements of the actual segment this code indicates the measured content of a package.
CV: Item weight considering its maximum possible humidity.
CZ: To specify length of core on which product is to be placed.
PRS: Measurement identifying the amount an item has been stretched prior to use.
XH: The height of the removable sides of a flat bed truck.
BSW: The measured breaking strength when wet.
BSY: The number of identified units per package.
BSZ: Number of units of a product or package within one layer of a package, container, etc.
DR: The measured fineness of a material.
DW: The measured width of a boxcar door.
VGM: The gross mass (weight) of the transport equipment verified according to SOLAS Chapter VI, Regulation 2, paragraphs 4-6.
BTA: A code used to indicate the weight per running metre of floor coverings over floor area.
BTB: A code used to indicate the weight per square metre of floor coverings over floor area.
BTC: The meat's acid quality or condition.
BTE: Maximum number of items stackable upon each other, including the bottom item.
BTF: Number of units of a product or package which make up the width of a layer in a package, container, pallet, etc.
BTG: Number of units of a product or package which make up the depth of a layer in a package, container, pallet, etc.
BTH: Extent expressed as a percentage to which an item can be nested within an identical item, e.g. paper cups.
BTI: Weight (mass) of goods including packaging and the carrier's equipment. In this context 'carrier's equipment' means any material resources necessary to facilitate the transport and handling of the goods without having the ability to move by its own propulsion, e.g. pallet, container, etc.
BTK: The lowest temperature at which polymerization may occur for a substance as packed for transport.
BTL: The lowest temperature at which self-accelerating decomposition may occur for a substance as packed for transport.
BTM: The controlled transport temperature to avoid decomposition of self-reactive substances and organic peroxides.
WA: The weight per unit of an area.
BRK: Maximum weight allowed to be stowed on top of an item during transport.
ADU: The end position from the beginning of an item located in the width direction.
WM: The maximum distance from side to side.
FI: Used e.g. in textile, print industries.
AAA: [6160] Weight of goods including any packaging that normally going with the goods.
